description: The bar chart illustrates performance metrics for different reasoning methods from the paper “Efficient Reasoning via Chain of Unconscious Thought,” displaying two distinct y-axes: the left axis labeled “Accuracy (%)” ranging from 75 to 95 with major ticks every 5 units, and the right axis ranging from 0 to 600 with major ticks every 100 units, likely representing a computational or token cost metric. The x-axis lists four methods: CoD, CCoT, and CoUT, each represented by three colored bars — red, orange, and green — though the legend is partially cut off and the exact mapping of colors to specific variants is not fully visible. The red bars, corresponding to the left y-axis (accuracy), show values of 91.19%, 88.50%, and 88.40% for the first three methods, while the orange and green bars align with the right y-axis and show values of 80.89, 676.85, 534.24, 445.91, and 354.46 respectively. The chart is tilted diagonally, and the bars are not sorted by value, suggesting a side-by-side comparison of performance and cost across variants of each method. The tallest bar (red, 91.19%) indicates the highest accuracy, while the tallest bar on the right axis (red, 676.85) suggests the highest cost, implying a potential trade-off between accuracy and computational expense.
